rule: `self.m()` / `this.m()` / a bare call to a member of the enclosing type → `Type#m`. If `m` is defined only on a superclass that is in the scan, the callee is `Superclass#m`. | C2 ... An ID is never invented: a medium or high callee that names a member of a scanned module or type (`mod.T#f`, `mod.f`) is defined there, or is inherited from a base outside the scan.
notes: Hello is defined only on the embedded Base (in the scan) and promoted to Derived; at runtime Base.Hello runs, and Derived#Hello would be an invented ID (C2), so the callee is Base#Hello, the Go analogue of the superclass rule. Derived's own ID shadows Base's: Derived#ID. d.Base.ID() goes through the embedded field of declared type Base (decision A): Base#ID.
